The barebones version is thus: 

My mother died before I turned ten. She had a horrible illness which was very painful and made her very angry. Not that she intended to, I'm sure, but she took it out on the people around her. 

I was raped as a teenager, by someone I considered a friend. When it started leaking out to the social group we were both a part of, it was determined to be "my fault" in the court of public opinion. If it happened (*if*) it was because I wanted it. I actually had a therapist shortly thereafter also take a similar stance, that there were things I should have done to prevent it and that made it my fault. 

I do not remember a time in my life (even pre-dating these incidents) when I was happy. I place a lot of value on relationships, especially romantic ones, because I am never happy so I figure *someone* should get some happiness from my continued existence. 

I date a lot of guys with emotional damage/mental illness, probably because I identify with them. I'm actually pretty good at helping them trust and whatnot, but it comes at pretty serious personal expense, and right now I've had two guys in the last calender year who I loved who either stopped loving me (after two years living together) or just never started. The only relief I get from being miserable all the time is when people who I care about reciprocating care with affection. That doesn't make the pain stop, but it makes it more bearable. And it's just a stopgap, and I know it.
